alex (devex): Quick Q — trying to script auth for CI. Which creds take precedence: REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, REDWOOD_PROFILE, or ~/.redwood/config.yaml? Also how does the CLI decide between system keyring vs file?

maria (sdk): Precedence is: 1) explicit flags (e.g. --profile / --api-key), 2) env vars (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_PROFILE), 3) credential helper / keyring, 4) config file (~/.redwood/config.yaml).

maria (sdk): Example config snippet we parse in the CLI:```yaml
profiles:
  default:
    api_key: ""
  ci:
    api_key: "file:/etc/rdw/ci_token"
    region: "us-west-2"
selected_profile: default
```

alex (devex): ah ok. so if I set REDWOOD_API_KEY in the env it will win over profile in config?

maria (sdk): yup. REDWOOD_API_KEY overrides. If you set REDWOOD_PROFILE, the CLI will try to load that profile from config or credential helper unless an API key env var is present.

sam (infra): Keyring behavior: on macOS we default to macOS keychain. Linux tries libsecret (gnome-keyring) then falls back to a file backend under ~/.local/share/rdw/creds (encrypted if possible). In CI we usually recommend using a file-based token or env var.

sam (infra): You can force file backend for noninteractive environments:```bash
rdw configure credential-backend file --path /etc/rdw/creds
# or set env for single-run:
export REDWOOD_CREDENTIAL_BACKEND=file
export REDWOOD_CREDENTIAL_PATH=/etc/rdw/creds
```

alex (devex): Nice. Any recommended minimal CI script for GitHub Actions?

maria (sdk): Minimal pattern we use in customers:```yaml
- name: Set Redwood token
  run: |
    echo "${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}" > /tmp/rdw_token
    export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /tmp/rdw_token)
- name: Call CLI
  run: rdw run --no-stream --prompt "hello"
```

maria (sdk): --no-stream is handy in CI so you get the full response and standard retry semantics (streaming has special socket semantics).

jing (platform): FYI: if you need deterministic retries for batch jobs, set CLI options: --retry-max 5 and --retry-backoff 2s (we also read CLI_RETRY_MAX and CLI_RETRY_BACKOFF env vars). Streaming endpoints may reconnect differently, so for automated pipelines prefer non-streamed requests.

alex (devex): good call. any gotchas on Windows runners?

sam (infra): Windows uses Credential Manager by default. For Docker-based runners, the container won't have access to host keyring, so use file or env. Also note file permissions: make sure /etc/rdw/creds (or wherever) is root:root 600 in prod.

alex (devex): thanks — last one: is there a helper to programmatically write a profile from a script?

maria (sdk): yes: `rdw credentials write --profile ci --api-key "${TOKEN}"` will store it using the configured backend. For pure file backend you can also write the YAML yourself but prefer the CLI helper so it respects encryption/keyring.

alex (devex): perfect. I will use env var for GH actions, and rdw credentials write for our internal deploys. thanks! :thumbsup:

rdw-cred-bot: credential-backend changed to file at /etc/rdw/creds (requested by alex (devex)) :white_check_mark:
